claims.head: Stay out of the box, Oilers
claims.call: The Red Wings’ power play creates at least their usual 9.1 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Red Wings’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Oilers’ kill is near the bottom. Every trip to the box hurts the Oilers more than most.

claims.head: Expect a grind
claims.call: The game’s pace score is below 97, slower than either team’s usual.
claims.see: Fewer than 64 shots between them at 5-on-5, on goal or wide, which usually means 54 or fewer shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: The Red Wings play some of the league’s slowest games, and so do the Oilers. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.

claims.head: Active D vs. Forward-led
claims.body: The Oilers’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Red Wings’ not so much. Edmonton is one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Detroit is near the bottom. Watch the Oilers’ defensemen jump into the play.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 8 of their last 10 games, including the last one. J.T. Compher takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Andreas Englund is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Johansson and Faulk.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 47% of the team’s power-play time in 11 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, down from 30% last season.

stakes: The Red Wings go in tied for seventh in the Atlantic with 11 points, the Oilers tied for first in the Pacific with 17 points.

EDM.head: The Oilers start a half-step ahead
EDM.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Red Wings can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

DET.head: The Red Wings start a half-step behind
DET.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Red Wings can tip it if their power play gets going.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Red Wings come in at 4-4-3, the Oilers at 8-2-1.
The Red Wings’ power play has a soft target in the Oilers’ kill. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey.

items.text: The Red Wings are newly without Daniil Tarasov, and have had to make do without Simon Edvinsson all season. Michal Postava is expected to start.
The Oilers are newly without Mattias Ekholm, and have had to make do without Matt Savoie all season.
Leon Draisaitl has a point in five straight games against Detroit, and 9 points in his last six against them.
With Jason Dickinson out, Colton Dach took eight faceoffs in the Oilers’ last game. He had been taking about two a game.
